rulings.invoke-1793542095075-9334-58a36f8a:
Exclude the whole-field pins from the choice-input digest. The digest exists so Q6 can see an unchanged choice situation; a digest over the pass and input bytes changes on every click and would let a repeat after refusal through, which is the defect the L4b map noted of the current field-wide digest.

Rule: the choice-input digest covers exactly what determined the comparison's outcome. Include the class ids as the set of (prediction digest, G units) pairs, the abstention G units, the forbidden set, the retained focus, the library pin (which fixes the menu) and the kernel pin (which fixes the model). Exclude the reading and graph pins; they stay in `:construction` where they already are, and the record lists under `:choice-input-digest :covers` exactly the inputs hashed and under `:excludes` the two pins with the reason "whole-field pins change on every click; the field enters the digest through the classes it produces".

Test as you proposed: with the construction pins fixed and a fact carrier changed on a task that moves no class's prediction or G, the digest is unchanged; a change that moves any class's pick, prediction or G changes it; a change to the forbidden set or the focus changes it. Keep the field-wide digest the inner Q6 uses untouched; this one is the selection run's.
rulings.invoke-1793542163468-9336-f8410b4d:
Both answers.

1. Keep the retention limit in this packet, explicit and typed. Reuse the predecessor and its sealed record for completed prior ticks; where the previous outer selection refused and left no record, `:previous` carries `{:status :absent :reason :refused-selection-left-no-record}` and the projector emits the Q6 carriers as not recomputable with that reason. Do not build the history writer here. It is needed, because a refused selection repeated on unchanged inputs is exactly the case Q6 exists for and today that refusal leaves nothing behind; the plan's principle is two runs per click, each a RunFacts, refused or not. That is the next packet, L5-4f: the selection run writes its own record on every click, including when the click stops at an outer refusal, and the previous-selection reader then prefers it. Name in your bell the point in the runtime where the outer refusal returns, so L5-4f is written from your reading.

2. Yes, include the class representative's pick in the digest beside the (prediction digest, G units) pairs. The class identifies the policy; the pick is what the choice enacts, and two situations whose classes coincide but whose picks differ are not the same choice. Record it under `:covers` like the rest.
